text.p: Segaworld, the world's biggest indoor theme park with 110,000 square feet (10,000 sq metres) of rides and games in the heart of London, opens on Sunday, promising to be an urban rival to the likes of Disneyworld.

Spread over seven floors in three buildings, the 45 million pound ($70 million) "futuractive" funfair at Piccadilly Circus features six interactive rides, a sports arena, the cockpit of a Harrier jump jet, a race track, a Coney Island-type carnival and a military combat zone.

"It's an urban version of the traditional theme park," Segaworld's James Bidwell told Reuters. "We have a strong location in the heart of London and the technology to deliver exciting experiences in a small space."

After entering the theme park on a rocket escalator, visitors can explore space in the year 2003 on the virtual reality Space Mission or plunge into the ocean depths wearing 3D glasses on the Aqua Planet.

If eerie rides through a monster's lair on the Beast of Darkness or an interactive Ghost Hunt are too ghoulish, there are race simulation rides, life-size video games and more traditional arcade-style entertainment.
Eighteen months in the making, operators claim Segaworld will provide enough attractions to entertain the most active children and adults for hours.
Open every day except Christmas, from morning to midnight, Segaworld expects to attract at least 1.75 million visitors, propelling it to the top of London's tourist attractions.
"It's a big development in the leisure business and adds a new dimension to family entertainment," said Bidwell.

Segaworld is hoping that Britain's traditional rainy weather and its state of the art technology together with what is billed as a modest admission charge of 12 pounds ($19) for adults and nine pounds ($14) for children will be enough to fill its 3,000 person capacity.
The London theme park could be the first of many by the Japanese electronic entertainment group. Bidwell said the group is already considering other sites but no locations have been announced.
But industry sources said Sega plans to challenge Walt Disney Co on its own turf and is considering a theme park in Las Vegas and sites in Hong Kong, Singapore and Sydney, Australia.
By concentrating on high technology for its rides and games, Sega said it is keeping costs lower than other entertainment theme park giants such as Disney and Universal Studios. ($1=.6385 Pound)
